english.title: Aid / abet a person to threaten with a blade / sharply pointed article in a public place
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) aided, abetted, counselled or procured **(..SPECIFY PERSON THREATENING..), to have

(A)_[an article which had a blade or was sharply pointed, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..),]_
(B)_[a folding pocket knife which had a blade the cutting edge of which exceeded 7.62 centimetres or three inches]_

with

(C)_[him]_
(D)_[her]_

in a public place, and to unlawfully and intentionally threaten another person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON THREATENED..), with that

(E)_[article,]_
(F)_[pocket knife,]_

in such a way that a reasonable person who was exposed to the same threat would think that there was an immediate risk of physical harm to that reasonable person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 139AA(1) and (6) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 and section 8 of the Accessories and Abettors Act 1861.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
aided, abetted, counselled or procured a person
to have with him / her
in a public place

english.notes:
(i) Section 139AA(5) states a 'public place' has the same meaning as in section 139. Section 139(7) defines 'public place' as any place to which at the material time the public have or are permitted access, whether on payment or otherwise.
(ii) Section 139AA(2) states an 'article' has the same meaning as section 139. Section 139(2) and (3) defines an article as one with a blade or was sharply pointed or a folding pocket knife which had a blade the cutting edge of which exceeded 7.62 centimetres or three inches.
(iii) Section 139AA was amended to insert an objective element into the offence; for offences committed before 6th April 2022 see H7244.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 4 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 139AA(6)(a) and (10) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

For minimum sentence for this offence see section 312 of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
